Second, Hesiod indicates that Prometheus was also punished for attempting to deceive Zeus by dividing sacrificial portions unfairly at Mecone, trying to trick Zeus into accepting inferior portions [2]. His punishment involved being bound with inextricable chains and having an eagle devour his liver daily, which would regenerate each night [3].

Odysseus escaped Polyphemus through a two-part plan [1][2]. First, he blinded the Cyclops by sharpening a club, heating it in fire, and using it to blind him [1][2]. When Polyphemus called out for help from other Cyclopes, they misunderstood his cries of "Nobody" and left him alone [1][2]. Second, after the blinding, Odysseus tied the Cyclops's rams together in groups of three and hid himself beneath the largest ram by clinging to its fleece [1][2]. When Polyphemus opened the cave door in the morning to let his flocks out to pasture, he felt the sheep as they passed but could not detect Odysseus hidden underneath [1][2]. Odysseus then escaped with his surviving comrades, drove the sheep to the ships, and sailed away [1][2].

Arachne was a mortal weaver of extraordinary skill who refused to acknowledge Athena's superiority in the art of weaving [1]. When Athena, disguised as an old woman, advised Arachne to show humility and ask the goddess for pardon, Arachne scornfully rejected her and challenged the goddess to a weaving contest [1]. After Arachne lost the contest, Athena destroyed her work in rage at Arachne's skill and struck her repeatedly [2]. When Arachne attempted to hang herself in despair, Athena saved her life but transformed her into a spider, declaring that she would 'dangle on a cord' forever and that her 'posterity forever shall take your example, that your punishment may last forever' [3].

Prometheus was punished for two main transgressions: first, he stole fire and gave it to humans, hiding it in a stalk of fennel without Zeus's knowledge [1][2]; second, he attempted to deceive Zeus by dividing sacrificial portions unfairly, placing flesh and organs covered with fat for the other gods while giving Zeus only white bones dressed with fat [1][2]. As punishment, Zeus ordered Hephaestus to bind Prometheus to Mount Caucasus with inextricable bonds and set an eagle upon him to devour his liver daily, which would regenerate each night [1]. This torment lasted many years until Heracles eventually freed him [1].

responses_by_run.answer: Odysseus escaped Polyphemus through a two-part plan. First, he blinded the Cyclops by sharpening a wooden club, heating it in fire, and driving it into Polyphemus's eye with the help of his comrades [1][2]. When Polyphemus cried out for help from other Cyclopes, they misunderstood his cries of "Nobody" and left him alone [1][2]. Second, after the blinding, Odysseus tied the Cyclops's rams together in groups of three and hid himself underneath the largest ram by clinging to its fleece [1][2]. When Polyphemus opened the cave door to let his flocks out to pasture, he felt the sheep as they passed but could not detect the men hidden beneath them [1][2]. Odysseus and his comrades thus escaped with the sheep to their ship [1][2].

At the wedding of Peleus and Thetis, the gods celebrated the marriage with feast and song on Mount Pelion [1]. The marriage took place after Peleus seized Thetis despite her shape-shifting resistance, holding her fast as she transformed into fire, water, and various beasts until she resumed her original form [1]. As wedding gifts, Chiron gave Peleus an ashen spear [1], and Poseidon gave him immortal horses named Balius and Xanthus [1].

Demeter stopped the crops from growing because she was grief-stricken and angry over the abduction of her daughter [1]. She vowed that she would never let fruit spring out of the ground until she beheld her own fair-faced daughter with her eyes [2].
